speaker: Andre
text_en: I wanted to ask history a question. Not what happened — what it felt like to hear what came next.

speaker: Caesar, offscreen
text_en: Does my name survive?

speaker: Andre
text_en: It survives. People still study the victories and the reforms. They also study what one man's power did to a republic.

speaker: Caesar, offscreen
text_en: Then they remember a tyrant?

speaker: Andre
text_en: They remember a question. Could the republic survive you? They are still asking it — about other men.

speaker: Khan, offscreen
text_en: Will my sons keep what I have made?

speaker: Andre
text_en: They will make it larger than you can picture. Merchants, ideas, and knowledge will cross it. So will the news of cities that are no longer there.

speaker: Khan, offscreen
text_en: And what will they call me?

speaker: Andre
text_en: Founder. Conqueror. Both words are still fighting over you. Neither one can make the dead speak.

speaker: Galileo, offscreen
text_en: Am I finally believed?

speaker: Andre
text_en: Believed, taught — and turned into a simple story: one man against the whole world. The truth was harder, and more interesting.

speaker: Galileo, offscreen
text_en: And what survives of the question?

speaker: Andre
text_en: Your observations. And one lesson from your trial that people keep relearning: silencing a man does not settle a question.

speaker: Napoleon, offscreen
text_en: Does France keep my laws?

speaker: Andre
text_en: Your code outlives your throne. Other nations borrow from it. It promises equality — and still finds people to leave out.

speaker: Napoleon, offscreen
text_en: And you. Where you come from — do they still argue about the price?

speaker: Andre
text_en: Every day. We are still not sure who pays it.

speaker: Oppenheimer, offscreen
text_en: Does the test work?

speaker: Andre
text_en: It works. Three weeks later, Hiroshima. Three days after that, Nagasaki. The war ends that summer. What it cost — and whether it had to — people are still asking.

speaker: Oppenheimer, offscreen
text_en: Can you tell me whether it was right?

speaker: Andre
text_en: I can tell you what came next. I can't tell you that.

speaker: Andre
text_en: I went looking for answers. I came back with their question. One day someone will sit across from us, knowing what came next. What will they have to tell us?
